title: The notebook as a way of thinking
description: On Leonardo, unfinished thinking, and why a notebook should be more than storage.

paragraphs.text: A notebook is not simply a place to put what we already know. It is a place to discover what we are trying to say. The page gives a thought somewhere to go before it knows what it is.

In Leonardo’s notebooks, a question about water can sit beside a drawing of a hand. There is no obligation to finish one thought before beginning another. “Describe the tongue of the woodpecker,” he reminds himself.[1]
I want this notebook to work in a similar way: a place where a drawing can interrupt an essay, where an observation can become a question, and where changing my mind leaves a trace.
